tikicchaka.p: [Kita+cha+ṇvu] (pu) CL=7 [Kita rogāpanayane, bhūvādi. Tikicchatīti tikicchako, cha-paccayo, ṇvu, dvittādi. Dhāna, ṭī. 329.(cikīpaka-saṃ). Tikicchako(pa,e)-apa, 1. 211, 349. Apa, 2. 4. Milinda. 172. Udāna, ṭṭha. 241. Aṃ, ṭī, 3. 337. Dhāna. Dhāna, ṭī. 329. Tikicchakā-aṃ, 3. 433-4. Jā,  356. Jā, ṭṭha, 2. 197. Jā, ṭṭha, 4. 500, 503. Tikicchakaṃ-milinda. 291. Cariyā, ṭṭha. 45. Tikicchake-peta, ṭṭha. 216. Tikicchakehi(ta,ba)- thera, ṭṭha, 2. 85. Tikicchakānaṃ(ca,ba)-peta, ṭṭha. 221. Tikicchakassa(cha,e)-milinda. 263. Tikicchake-buddhavaṃ. 307. Abhi, ṭṭha, 1. 35. Buddhavaṃ, ṭṭha, 93. Jā, ṭṭha, 1. 6.] Can cure, One who can cure, (A) (Practitioner of indigenous medicine (or) Doctor) who can heal the sore or disease of the body. (B) (Lord Buddha) who can heal or reject the Kilesā disease, (C) (A Thera) who was named Tikicchaka.

[ကိတ+ဆ+ဏွု။ ကိတ ရောဂါပနယနေ၊ ဘူဝါဒိ။ တိကိစ္ဆတီတိ တိကိစ္ဆကော၊ ဆ-ပစ္စယော၊ ဏွု၊ ဒွိတ္တာဒိ။ ဓာန်၊ ဋီ။ ၃၂၉။ （စိကီပက-သံ）။ တိကိစ္ဆကော （ပ၊ဧ）-အပ၊ ၁။ ၂၁၁၊ ၃၄၉။ အပ၊ ၂။ ၄။ မိလိန္ဒ။ ၁၇၂။ ဥဒါန၊ ဋ္ဌ။ ၂၄၁။ အံ၊ ဋီ၊ ၃။ ၃၃၇။ ဓာန်။ ဓာန်၊ ဋီ။ ၃၂၉။ တိကိစ္ဆကာ-အံ၊ ၃။ ၄၃၃-၄။ ဇာ၊ ၏။ ၃၅၆။ ဇာ၊ ဋ္ဌ၊ ၂။ ၁၉၇။ ဇာ၊ ဋ္ဌ၊ ၄။ ၅ဝဝ၊ ၅ဝ၃။ တိကိစ္ဆကံ-မိလိန္ဒ။ ၂၉၁။ စရိယာ၊ ဋ္ဌ။ ၄၅။ တိကိစ္ဆကေ-ပေတ၊ ဋ္ဌ။ ၂၁၆။ တိကိစ္ဆကေဟိ （တ၊ဗ）- ထေရ၊ ဋ္ဌ၊ ၂။ ၈၅။ တိကိစ္ဆကာနံ （စ၊ဗ）-ပေတ၊ ဋ္ဌ။ ၂၂၁။ တိကိစ္ဆကဿ （ဆ၊ဧ）-မိလိန္ဒ။ ၂၆၃။ တိကိစ္ဆကေ-ဗုဒ္ဓဝံ။ ၃ဝ၇။ အဘိ၊ ဋ္ဌ၊ ၁။ ၃၅။ ဗုဒ္ဓဝံ၊ ဋ္ဌ၊ ၉၃။ ဇာ၊ ဋ္ဌ၊ ၁။ ၆။]

tikicchanta.p: [Kita+cha+anta] (ti) CL=7 [Ti-kicchanto(pa,e)-vi,ṭṭha,1.160. Udāna, ṭṭha. 154. Apa, ṭṭha, 1. 141. Apa, ṭṭha, 2. 184. Ti-kicchantā-jā, ṭṭha, 7. 375. Tikicchantaṃ(du,e)-thera. 288. Saṃ, ṭṭha, 1. 210. 314. Thera, ṭṭha, 2. 113, 115. Netti, ṭṭha. 257. Saṃ, ṭī, 1. 256, 333. Tikicchantānaṃ(cha,ba)-saṃ, 1. 164-5, 224-5. Netti. 150. Saṃ, ṭṭha, 1. 210, 314. Netti, vi. 328. Tikicchataṃ-saṃ, ṭṭha, 1. 210(syā).] (1) Can heal (A) It can heal the disease of the physical body. (B) It can reject and cease the mind disease which is Kilesā. (C) It can block and prohibit the danger which is non-benefit. (D) It has completed the beneficial matter. (E) One who tolerates for anger.

tikicchā.cp: fem. the art of healing; practice of medicine.
tikicchā.p: [Kita+cha+ā] (thī) CL=7 [Kaccaññaḥ. 638. Nīti, sutta. 1250. Kita+cha+a+ā. Rū.599. Moga, 5. 2. Dhāna, ṭī. 330. Sūci.(cikitā-saṃ)] (1) Healing, (A) It has healed the disease of the physical body. (2) Healing which removes the spikes which pierce through (in the body or mind).  See -  tikicchāvuṭṭhāpana. (3) It heals the disease by medicine which is like the prescribed body. (4) Healing the person who was bewitched (catched ) by demon infesting the earth. There is five kinds of healing which is taking care for a young man.

tikicchana.p: [Kita+cha+yu] (na) CL=7 (1) Medical treatment (or) Give medical treatment (or) Give medicine to others for using., (A) It heals completely the disease of the body. (B) Rejects and ceases the danger which is non-benefit issue. See - Tikicchanattha-(B). (C) Healing and frightens. (D) Healing which is clean and cheerful. (E) Heals and tolerates a Kilesā which is a mind disease. (Ti) (2) One who has the nature of healing the disease which is a Kilesā disease.
